messages:
PagerDuty: :rotating_light: HIGH: Elevated egress packet loss and BGP withdraws observed from us-east-1 to upstream providerX. Incident INC-2198765432 created. Link: https://pagerduty.local/incidents/INC-2198765432

PagerDuty: Paging Maya (on-call)

Maya (on-call): ack. seeing spike in p95 generation latency and increased 504s for us-east-1 since ~04:18 UTC.

Maya (on-call): adding Sam (NetOps) and Jordan (SRE) into channel. @Liam-CS FYI for customer notif.

Sam (NetOps): BGP view from our collectors shows rapid withdraws from providerX peers and neighbor resets.
```
BGP peer 203.0.113.45 Flaps: 6 Last change 00:03:10
Prefixes received: 1100 -> 920
```

Sam (NetOps): traceroute from edge -> providerX shows intermittent loss on their mid-tier hop.
```
traceroute to 8.8.8.8
 1 10.1.1.1 0.4 ms
 2 203.0.113.2 12.1 ms
 3 203.0.113.18 120.4 ms  * 120.7 ms  <-- 33% packet loss
```

Jordan (SRE): impact summary — generation endpoints p95 jumped from ~200ms to ~1s, error rate up ~4%. us-east-2 can handle failover load but sessions stick to us-east-1 until DNS/conn resets.

Liam (CS): getting customer reports about slow inference and a handful of timed-out API calls. I'm preparing targeted comms for customers on us-east-1 capacity.

Maya (on-call): mitigation plan — quick wins then durable fixes:
- lower DNS TTL for region endpoints from 300 -> 60s to accelerate client re-resolve
- enable edge-session-handoff so new sessions prefer us-east-2 for affected orgs
- ask NetOps to open ticket with providerX NOC and request emergency working group
- if providerX can't stabilize, announce backup paths via providerY and shift critical prefixes

Sam (NetOps): opened SR-100921 with providerX and posted BGP dumps. providerX NOC responded: "we're seeing control-plane instability on POP-3, investigating." They requested full RIB snapshots.

Infra-Bot: DNS TTL change queued by Maya.

Maya (on-call): applying DNS TTL change now and enabling edge-session-handoff override for orgs with high error counts.

Sam (NetOps): preparing to prepend / announce more specific prefixes to steer via providerY. Planned command:
```
configure bgp
neighbor 198.51.100.23 route-map OUT permit 10
set community 65000:200
commit
```
Will execute after green check from SRE.

Jordan (SRE): stand by — validating that us-east-2 capacity > incoming shift. Running synthetic load tests.

Sam (NetOps): providerX NOC: "we applied control-plane fix on POP-3; monitoring; will follow up with root-cause." They are still seeing occasional withdraws.

Jordan (SRE): after TTL + handoff changes, we're seeing traffic shift and p95 down to ~320ms. Error rate trending down to ~1.2%. In-flight sessions still affected until clients reconnect.

Liam (CS): sent interim customer advisory to top-15 affected tenants with suggested workaround (retry/backoff) and ETA 30 minutes for stabilization.

Sam (NetOps): executed announce via providerY for critical prefixes. BGP summary shows established neighbor and accepted routes.

Sam (NetOps): BGP after announce:
```
Neighbor 198.51.100.23 Established 00:01:45, routes advertised: 56
Accepted: 1120
Withdraws down
```

Jordan (SRE): metrics now stable: p95 generation latency ~260ms, error rate 0.5%. No new alerts on error budget. Monitoring for recurrence.

Maya (on-call): incident state -> MITIGATED. We'll keep pages suppressed for 1h. Collecting artifacts for postmortem.

Sam (NetOps): providerX confirmed they've stabilized the control-plane and will provide an RCA. We'll retain more-specifics until we confirm no regression.

Maya (on-call): action items:
- Sam: upload final BGP/rib dumps and route-change timeline (owner: Sam)
- Jordan: full synthetic test matrix + rollback/playbook for session-handoff (owner: Jordan)
- Liam: send final customer impact email with timelines and mitigation steps (owner: Liam)
- Maya: create incident doc and schedule postmortem in 48h (owner: Maya)

Infra-Bot: Incident INC-2198765432 status updated -> MITIGATED. Responders: Maya, Sam, Jordan, Liam.

Maya (on-call): closing thread here. Postmortem will include BGP logs, traceroutes, DNS TTL changes, smart-routing overrides, and customer impact table. Thanks all :white_check_mark:

Jordan (SRE): attaching traffic-shift and per-prefix graphs to the incident doc. I'll include a note about session stickiness.

Sam (NetOps): I'll monitor for 24h and coordinate with providerX for any scheduled maintenance.

Liam (CS): customer follow-ups queued.

Maya (on-call): thread closed. Good job team.
